scenes.line1: How fast is your code, really?
scenes.say: How fast is your code, really? Can you prove it in an interview?

scenes.label: Big-O
scenes.sub: Describes the upper bound of time or space as input grows.
scenes.say: Big O describes the upper bound of your algorithm's time or space as the input grows.
In interviews, always state both time and space complexity. Say if it's worst case, average, or amortized.

scenes.title: Python List Append
lines: $ # O(1) most times, O(n) when resizing
scenes.say: For example, appending to a Python list is usually constant time, but resizing can make it linear in rare cases. That's why we call it amortized constant time.

scenes.question: What does Big-O actually describe?
scenes.right: Big O shows how time or space grows as input gets larger.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: Big O does not give the exact running time. It shows how time or space grows as input gets larger.
